chapter: SHRM BASK: Financial Metrics & Revenue Analytics
scenario: In hotel operational analytics, which financial metric measures total room revenue divided by total available rooms over a given period?
explanation: RevPAR combines occupancy rate and average daily rate to evaluate overall room inventory yield performance.
memory_anchor: 🏨 RevPAR = Room Revenue ÷ Total Available Rooms (or Occupancy % × ADR).

chapter: SHRM BASK: OSHA General Duty & Energy Control
scenario: A 1,500-room luxury hotel casino experiences an OSHA inspection after a facilities maintenance technician suffers an electrical burn injury while servicing an exhaust fan without applying Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) protocols. The inspector cites the General Duty Clause (Section 5(a)(1)). How should HR lead the response?
options: Audit all equipment energy-control procedures, mandate LOTO retraining for facilities staff, and strictly enforce documented safety compliance.
Claim full legal immunity because safety protocols were reviewed during initial employee onboarding two years prior.
Reclassify all maintenance staff as independent contractors to transfer liability away from resort operations.
Issue an oral reprimand to the technician and close the internal incident file.
explanation: Under Section 5(a)(1) of the OSH Act, employers must furnish a workplace free from recognized hazards likely to cause death or serious physical harm. HR must conduct immediate energy control audits, retrain workers, and enforce compliance.
memory_anchor: ⚠️ OSHA Response = Audit energy controls, retrain staff, and strictly enforce documented LOTO compliance.

scenario: Which quantitative job evaluation technique breaks positions down into compensable factors (such as skill, effort, responsibility, and working conditions) and assigns point values to determine internal pay grades?
explanation: The Point-Factor Method evaluates jobs quantitatively using weighted compensable factors to establish objective internal relative worth.
memory_anchor: 🔢 Point-Factor Method = Scoring positions quantitatively based on compensable factors.

chapter: SHRM BASK: Title VII & National Origin Discrimination
scenario: A resort General Manager mandates a strict 'English-Only at all times' policy covering all work time and non-work break periods across the housekeeping department, claiming it improves guest service. Housekeepers complain to HR. What is HR's best legal and strategic directive?
options: Advise the GM to rescind the blanket policy immediately, explaining that English-only rules during non-work breaks presumptively violate Title VII national origin protections unless strictly required by narrow business necessity during job performance.
Uphold the GM's policy to maintain operational consistency and guest experience standards.
Require non-English speaking employees to take unpaid English language courses off property.
Transfer complaining housekeepers to night-shift cleaning duties to eliminate guest interaction.
explanation: EEOC guidance establishes that blanket rules requiring employees to speak only English at all times, including non-work break periods, violate Title VII national origin protections unless justified by strict business necessity during job performance.
memory_anchor: 🗣️ English-Only = Rescind blanket rules; Title VII protects native languages during non-work break time.

chapter: SHRM BASK: ADDIE Instructional Design Model
scenario: In instructional design and workforce development, which phase of the ADDIE model involves setting learning objectives, constructing curriculum architecture, selecting delivery methods, and designing module assessments?
explanation: The Design phase of ADDIE establishes learning objectives, target audience requirements, course sequencing, media selection, and test design based on analysis findings.
memory_anchor: 📐 ADDIE Design = Constructing the curriculum blueprint and learning objectives before creating training materials.
